newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil Congress panel may vote on oil bill Tuesday.
newsitem.headline: Brazil Congress panel may vote on oil bill Tuesday.

text.p: A bill regulating the opening up of Brazil's petroleum monopoly to private companies might be put to a vote in a committee of the Chamber of Deputies Tuesday, a congressional official said.

Although classed as a discussion session, the official said tomorrow's meeting of the lower house committee might vote on the bill which sets down rules for private sector involvement in the oil and gas industries.
If approved in the panel, the bill goes to the floor of the Chamber of Deputies. It also requires approval in the Senate.

Brazil's Congress approved in 1995 a constitutional amendment to break up the production, refining and transportation monopoly enjoyed by state-owned Petrobras but has yet to approved enabling legislation.

The bill under study would allow Petrobras to maintain its rights to areas where it is already involved in production or exploration. As a result, private companies are expected to go into partnership with Petrobras rather than compete with it.
The new legislation also creates a new regulator, the National Petroleum Agency to oversee the sector and would allow foreign investors to buy voting shares in Petrobras.
